Guides

Queuing Systems

  • Simple Queue (M/M/1) — A single-server queuing system where items arrive randomly, wait in a queue, are processed by one server, and depart. This is the foundational discrete-event pattern for any service or processing system.
  • Multi-Server Queue (M/M/c) — A queuing system with multiple parallel servers sharing a single waiting line. Items wait in one queue and are routed to the next available server, modeling call centers, bank teller lines, or parallel machines.
  • Priority Queue — A queuing system where items are served in priority order rather than arrival order. High-priority items jump ahead of lower-priority items in the queue, modeling emergency services, VIP lanes, or job scheduling with urgency levels.
